prompts.display_text: Pin a country with ten or more of the Church's missions (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with ten or more of the Church's missions (end of 2025).
prompts.note: Next below the line: Guatemala, Japan, Ecuador and DR Congo with 7 each.
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 the United States had 120 of the Church's missions. Brazil (37), Mexico (34) and the Philippines (26) came next, and Peru, Argentina, Chile and Nigeria had 11 or more each. Nigeria and the Philippines were the only countries outside the Americas with ten or more.

prompts.display_text: Pin a non-Soviet Warsaw Pact country (today's borders) dedicated or rededicated for the gospel between 1977 and 2006
prompts.text_original: As communist rule eased and then ended, Church leaders dedicated or rededicated the former Soviet satellites of Europe for the preaching of the gospel. A country that was a Warsaw Pact member other than the Soviet Union (Poland, East Germany, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Albania), in its present-day form, dedicated or rededicated for preaching the gospel between 1977 and 2006.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Poland, Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Albania)
prompts.note: Germany does not count. Elder Nelson's 1990 Prague rededication counts for the Czech Republic; Slovakia had its own in 2006.
prompts.summary: Spencer W. Kimball rededicated Poland in 1977 while it was still communist. Russell M. Nelson dedicated Hungary in 1987, then Romania and Bulgaria and rededicated Czechoslovakia in early 1990. Dallin H. Oaks dedicated Albania in 1993, and Dieter F. Uchtdorf dedicated newly independent Slovakia in 2006.

answers.name: Poland
answers.fact: President Spencer W. Kimball rededicated Poland in Warsaw, August 24, 1977.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson rededicated Czechoslovakia in Prague, February 6, 1990.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Hungary on Gellert Hill, Budapest, April 19, 1987.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Romania in Cismigiu Park, Bucharest, February 8, 1990.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Bulgaria in Sofia, February 13, 1990.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: Elder Dallin H. Oaks dedicated Albania at Monument of Heroes Park, Tirana, April 23, 1993.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf dedicated Slovakia in Trencin, May 12, 2006.

prompts.display_text: Pin an Asian or Pacific country where a current General Authority Seventy once led a mission (October 2026).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies had led missions in Asia or the Pacific. Pin a country there where one of those missions was headquartered, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, General Authority Seventies had led missions in Japan, the Philippines, New Zealand, Taiwan and Thailand. Elder Michael John U. Teh, born in the Philippines, presided over the Taiwan Taichung Mission.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Japan Tokyo North and South missions (Elder Esplin) and Japan Tokyo South (Elder Wada).

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Philippines Quezon City Mission, 2013 to 2016 (Elder Revillo).

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: New Zealand Auckland Mission (Elder Carl B. Cook).

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Taiwan Taipei (Elder Perkins) and Taiwan Taichung (Elder Teh) missions.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: Elder Michael T. Ringwood was called in 2004 to lead the Korea Seoul West Mission.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Elder Kelly R. Johnson returned to the Thailand Bangkok Mission as a leader, 2015 to 2018.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country (Turkey counts) where Church histories place the first convert baptism on its soil in 1883-1899
prompts.text_original: A European country (Turkey counts) whose first convert baptism on its soil, per Church histories, came between 1883 and 1899.
prompts.citation: Church Global Histories chronologies: Austria, Czech Republic, Belgium, Russia, Romania; Church News country profile and Church History Topics: Turkey
prompts.note: Poland, Hungary and Serbia do not count: their first converts were baptized outside their borders.
prompts.summary: In the 1880s and 1890s missionaries carried the gospel into new corners of Europe. Church histories date first baptisms to Lambach, Austria (1883), Prague (1884), Constantinople (1885), Antwerp (1888), St. Petersburg (1895) and Constanta, Romania (1899).

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: 1883: first convert baptism in Austria, at Lambach.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: 1895: first convert baptism in St. Petersburg.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: 1888: first convert baptism in Belgium, at Antwerp.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: 1884: first convert baptized in Prague.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: January 4, 1885: Hagop Vartooguian and his family were baptized in Constantinople by Jacob Spori, days after the Turkish Mission opened.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: 1899: first convert baptized at Constanta on the Black Sea.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding part of the Jordan River, the sea of Chinnereth, or the Hermon springs that feed it
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding part of the Jordan River, the river Israel crossed under Joshua and Naaman washed in, including its sea of Chinnereth (Galilee) and the springs of Mount Hermon that feed it
prompts.note: Mount Hermon sits on the Lebanon-Syria border, and its springs feed the Jordan, so both count, as in the Song of Solomon prompt.
prompts.summary: The Jordan River gathers springs on the slopes of Mount Hermon, flows through the sea of Chinnereth (Galilee), and winds down to the salt sea. Israel crossed it on dry ground at Jericho under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha parted it, and Naaman the Syrian was healed by dipping in it seven times (Josh 3; 2 Kgs 2, 5).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The Jordan runs through the sea of Chinnereth, the Sea of Galilee, which lies in Israel (Deut 3:17; Bible Dictionary, Jordan River).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: The river forms Jordan's western border; Israel camped on its east bank before crossing (Josh 3:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The lower river near Jericho, where the waters stood up as an heap for Israel, borders the West Bank (Josh 3:16).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The Bible Dictionary says the Jordan is formed by several springs rising in Mount Hermon, a mountain on the Syria-Lebanon border.

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Those Hermon springs feed the Jordan, and Mount Hermon's western slopes lie in Lebanon (Bible Dictionary, Jordan River and Hermon).
